name: Heading
statusNote: Alpha in name only: Heading is a thin h1-h6 wrapper with three type presets and has been stable for several majors. The docs list no stories.
summary: A section heading: an h1-h6 element set in one of the title presets. Choose the element for the document outline and the variant for the visual weight, independently; use Text for running copy.

inputs.name: level
inputs.description: The heading element (the as prop). It sets the outline level only; it does not change the size.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: The title preset. With none the heading is 32px semibold in the inherited family and line height.

anatomy.name: Heading
anatomy.description: One text run, no margin, in the inherited foreground colour.

variants.description: 32px (--text-title-size-large) semibold; family and line height come from the surroundings (BaseStyles gives 1.5).
Title large: 32px over 48px, semibold, system stack.
Title medium: 20px over 32.5px, semibold, system stack.
Title small: 16px over 24px, semibold, system stack.

layout.text: The heading has no margin; spacing around it is the container's job. It wraps like any block text.
Without a variant the module sets only font size and weight; the line height and font family are inherited, so they follow the surrounding text (1.5 and the system stack under BaseStyles).
A variant sets the whole font through the title shorthand token, so size, line height, weight and family move together.

states.text: Static text in the inherited foreground colour; Heading sets no colour of its own.

behaviour.text: Heading renders the element named by as (h2 by default); in development it warns when that element is not an h1-h6.

semantics: Exposed as a heading at the level of its element (h1 is level 1); screen-reader users navigate by these levels.
The level must fit the page outline, whatever the visual variant.

notes.text: The heading level comes from the HTML element and reaches assistive technology through the browser. A native build must expose a heading role and its level to the platform accessibility API itself, separately from the visual variant.
Every rule sits inside :where(), so it has zero specificity: any class a caller adds overrides the size, weight and margin. A native port should treat a caller's style as winning outright.
No variant and variant large share size and weight but differ in line height and family: the default inherits them, large sets 48px and the system stack.
